title: Fix Windows command overflow in sparse baseline preflight
body:
The current selected-source inventory can make `research_baseline_sparse.py` reject a valid Windows sparse checkout. At canonical main `cef4b52f2a59009865bf8eabde1be3f159063703`, 503 omitted inputs produced a 38,351-character Git command and `WinError 206`. The helper then incorrectly reported the first genuine sparse omission as an invalid file.

Batch selected-input checks within a conservative 16,000 UTF-16-unit quoted-path budget, reusing the existing sparse/HEAD validator. Complete omission coverage, schema routing, ordinary-deletion and staged-drift rejection, and failure propagation are preserved. Five new real-Git regression cases exercise 600 paths, including spaces, literal brackets and supplementary Unicode, an actual CLI/materialization round trip, late invalid entries and a later Git failure.

Validation at `9a06fb2983202e951e294774a56a15c5a169867e`:

- All five new cases failed before the fix on Windows, including the unmocked CLI.
- All 14 sparse-baseline tests pass normally and under `-O` on native Windows / CPython 3.12.0; the same 14 pass on Ubuntu/WSL / CPython 3.12.3.
- After selected inputs were materialized, the preflight reports no omissions and the unchanged successor reports `PASS_RESEARCH_BASELINE_BINDINGS_ONLY`.
- All 6,136 top-level SOURCES/VERIFY manifests were checked against their committed blobs; none pins or declares the changed preflight. The exact committed-change planner recognizes all three changed paths and selects zero scientific packages.
- `git diff --check` passes.

The broader Windows helper run executed 362 tests: 322 passed, 22 skipped, and 18 encountered setup errors. Twelve use newline-containing filenames unsupported on Windows; six initially lacked a sparse fixture. After fixture/source hydration, three source-role methods still failed on native Windows at alternate-store historical-source resolution. All 18 affected methods passed on Ubuntu/WSL. These unchanged fixture limitations are documented; a clean full native Windows suite is not claimed. The full mathematical cold replay was not run.

This refines the `portable-replay` card (priority revision 7; nonce `1568f02fbdb6dc3102dbdeab4f3c4e6e`). [Canonical claim and coordination](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4458#discussioncomment-19136447). Final overlap covered 308 open PRs, 4,007 Discussion records and all 6,601 tracked local notes; it found this claim and the distinct fixture-maintenance predecessor. Canonical main was fetched again before publication and remained unchanged.

[Evidence, reproduction and remaining scope](https://github.com/mihir-s-05/integer-mult-bounds/blob/9a06fb2983202e951e294774a56a15c5a169867e/docs/research/sparse-baseline-windows-argv.md). The emitted directory-materialization command and other callers of the generic validator remain separate potential large-inventory boundaries. Selected kappa, frozen scientific inputs, the pinned chooser and baseline implementations are unchanged.

Credit Douglas Colkitt and the credited Claude/Mister-Meeseeks preflight (#3725), Arham-Tahir64's sparse contract (#3102), lee-phys's schema repair (#4631), Clear1nsight's fixture cleanup (#4857), and the retained onboarding contributors. Prepared by Mihir Srivastava with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; no subagents or independent human review. Apache-2.0.

Hosted validation subsequently **passed** for this exact PR head: [run 39891861128](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39891861128), job `plan`. Its Linux helper suite ran 362 tests in 142.993 seconds with 11 expected platform skips; the changed-package planner emitted `{"include": []}`, and scientific replay was correctly skipped. Local platform limitations above remain recorded. All three published files also passed a raw working/commit byte comparison, and the pushed branch resolves to the stated commit.
